title: Is Everest really the tallest mountain?
examples: Is Mauna Kea taller than Everest?
Which mountain is the tallest from bottom to top?
What does above sea level mean?

right.title: Mauna Kea
points: Base is deep under the sea

explain.say: Here is a puzzle for you. If two friends stand on different steps, who is taller? It depends where you measure from! Mountains are just the same. Look at the two mountains on the board.

draw.text: Is Everest really the tallest mountain?

right.title: Mauna Kea
points: Base is deep under the sea

explain.say: On the left is Mount Everest. Its top is 8,849 metres above sea level, which means above the height of the sea. No point on Earth reaches higher into the sky. Can you find its number?

right.title: Mauna Kea
points: Base is deep under the sea

explain.say: Now look at the right: Mauna Kea, a volcano in Hawaii. Above the sea it is only 4,207 metres. But its bottom is deep under the ocean! From bottom to top it is about 10,200 metres, taller than Everest.

right.title: Mauna Kea
points: Base is deep under the sea

explain.say: So Everest is the highest, but Mauna Kea is the tallest from base to top. See the verdict at the bottom? It depends how you measure. Which way do you think is fairer?

right.title: Mauna Kea
points: Base is deep under the sea

explain.say: Great thinking! One more surprise: Chimborazo in Ecuador has the top farthest from Earth's centre, because Earth bulges at the equator. Three mountains, three different winners!

faq.q: What does above sea level mean?
faq.a: It means measured from the average height of the sea. Mountains are usually measured this way, so we can compare them fairly all over the world.

faq.q: Is Mauna Kea taller than Everest?
faq.a: From its base on the sea floor to its top, Mauna Kea is about 10,200 metres, taller than Everest. But most of it is underwater, so above sea level it is only 4,207 metres.
asks: Which is taller, Mauna Kea or Everest?

faq.q: Which mountain is closest to space?
faq.a: Chimborazo in Ecuador. Earth is a little fatter at the equator, so its peak is about 2 kilometres farther from Earth's centre than Everest's.

faq.q: Why is Mauna Kea mostly underwater?
faq.a: Mauna Kea is a volcano that grew up from the deep floor of the Pacific Ocean, so its lower part is hidden under about 6,000 metres of water.

facts: Mauna Kea rises 4,207 metres above sea level but about 10,200 metres from its base on the ocean floor.
